newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco bourse down in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Morocco bourse down in low volume.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed on Wednesday 0.19 percent lower with few stocks traded and low volumes seen on both the official and over-the-counter markets, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse share index closed at 634.09 points from 635.28 points on Tuesday.
"The market is maintaining its gloomy trend with people cautious over buying shares," a Casablanca-based broker said.
ONA, the country's largest private holding edged down two dirhams to 770 dirhams with 52 shares traded.
shareholders earlier on Wednesday unanimously approved the 1996 consolidated results showing a net profit of $93.4 million.
SNI, the second largest private group, dipped five dirhams to 710 dirhams with 580 shares exchanged on the market.
Steel mill Sonasid also fell, shedding 10 dirhams to 540 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur closed unchanged at 580 dirhams.
Second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in May 1996, was up 13 dirhams to 1,188 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc rose one dirham to 858 dirhams.
Oil refinery Samir remained unchanged at 343 dirhams with 3,000 shares exchanged.
Total traded volume on the official market was 19.2 million dirhams from 17.2 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 4.6 million dirhams from 62.9 million dirhams with main trade in 6,589 Samir shares.
